int_name: N BROAD ST & W OXFORD ST

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility zebra crosswalk, pedestrian signals, and wide, well-maintained sidewalks. However, the wide roadway and lack of a median refuge or curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radius
hazards.description: The corner design allows for high-speed vehicle turns, increasing risk to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians are exposed to traffic for a significant distance without a refuge.

interventions.title: Curb Extension
interventions.description: Install a bulb-out to reduce crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to provide a safe waiting area.

result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and pedestrian signals. The environment features wide sidewalks and institutional buildings, but lacks physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions or medians to reduce crossing exposure.

hazards.name: Wide turning radii
hazards.description: The corners have wide radii which may encourage high-speed vehicle turns across the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire width of the street without a median refuge.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and dedicated pedestrian signals with curb ramps. However, the wide roadway and lack of a median refuge island increase exposure time for pedestrians crossing multiple lanes of traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median refuge island.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and wear in the asphalt within the marked crosswalk area could present a trip hazard.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the cracked asphalt within the crosswalk to ensure a smooth, level walking surface.

result.summary: The image shows a one-way urban street with a marked zebra crosswalk and curb ramps. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars on the left side of the street near the crosswalk may block the sight lines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, just beyond the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Missing pedestrian signal
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal head is visible at this signalized intersection, which can lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear crossing instructions.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines.
